annotations.text:
The core flows are live, not pictures — filters, checklists, photo tiles, the side-of-street toggle and the messaging dial all work.

Start at 1. The argument for the whole product is screen 2: flip to the other side of the street and watch an 18-minute emergency become a 2-day non-event. That gap is why the app asks instead of guessing.

Settled 15 Sep — full record in docs/design/01-decisions.md

• Messaging: Draft only. Auto-send would ride the extension, so it only fires when the laptop is open.
• Alerts: push only, with a "last alert delivered" heartbeat so silence is detectable. SMS behind a flag.
• Turo data: extension when Chrome is up, plus Gmail ingestion 24/7. Extensions don't run on phones.
• ASP: parse the citywide sign dataset, with capture-once as the fallback that ships first.
• Render + Google sign-in. 15–25 cars in 12 months, so Task carries an owner from day one.

Still open: does the Transit need its own parking rules?

The layered read: adapters are replaceable and never load-bearing, modules only emit Tasks, and the run sheet consumes nothing but Tasks.

That is what lets "car is out on a trip, so don't nag about street cleaning" be one rule instead of four modules knowing about each other.
